parts.title: Calorie Counting
parts.summary: Group blank-line-separated positive integer calorie items into per-Elf inventories, compute each Elf's total calories, and find the highest single-Elf calorie total.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass bounded top-k leaderboard scan (k = 1) over immutable ElfInventory value objects (computing totalCalories dynamically from raw items), verified against an independent descending-sort oracle and matching the pre-verified AoC star answer.
learnings: Generalizing rankTopElves and traceTopElves to parameter k in 2022/day01/shared/ handles Part 1 (k = 1) and Part 2 (k = 3) with zero parser or engine churn.
Computing totalCalories and itemCount via getters on frozen ElfInventory keeps raw snack items as the single source of truth.

parts.title: Calorie Counting
parts.summary: Using the same blank-line-separated Elf calorie inventories from Part 1, identify the three Elves carrying the highest individual totals and return their combined calorie sum.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2022/day01/shared rankTopElves(inventories, 3) and sumCalories: single-pass bounded top-3 insertion in O(N) time and O(1) extra space, differentially verified against a descending-sort oracle and matching the pre-verified AoC star answer.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) extra tracking space
learnings: Parameterizing the shared leaderboard engine by k let Part 2 achieve 100% coverage in 30 lines of domain code with zero imports from part1/.
Wrapping both parse and trace inside try/catch in the visualizer cleanly handles valid 1- or 2-Elf inputs that reject top-3 selection.

parts.title: Rock Paper Scissors
parts.summary: Score a Rock Paper Scissors strategy guide where A/B/C denote the opponent's Rock/Paper/Scissors and X/Y/Z denote your direct Rock/Paper/Scissors throw, summing shape points (1/2/3) plus outcome points (0/3/6) across all rounds.
parts.algorithmSummary: Cyclic Z_3 modular scoring via shared/core euclideanMod(player - opponent + 1, 3) with immutable StrategyRound, ResolvedRound, and 9-cell MatchupSummary value objects in 2022/day02/shared/; exhaustively tested across all 9 pairs and differentially verified against an explicit 3x3 rule matrix over 2,500 rounds.
learnings: Using shared/core euclideanMod(player - opponent + 1, 3) avoids JavaScript negative modulo bugs on Scissors vs Rock and mirrors Part 2's inverse formula.
Storing raw A/B/C and X/Y/Z tokens in StrategyRound plus a RoundResolver interface lets Part 2 reinterpret X/Y/Z as desired outcomes with zero parser churn.

parts.title: Rock Paper Scissors
parts.summary: Reinterpret column two (X/Y/Z) as the desired round outcome (Lose/Draw/Win), select the unique player shape achieving that outcome against A/B/C, and sum shape plus outcome points across all rounds.
parts.algorithmSummary: Modular inverse RoundResolver (DesiredOutcomeResolver) plugging into 2022/day02/shared with zero churn: derives playerShape = euclideanMod(opponent + desiredOutcome - 1, 3), verified across all 9 combinations and differentially checked against a hardcoded LUT oracle over 2,500 rounds.
learnings: Inverting the Z_3 outcome equation via shared/core euclideanMod(opponent + desiredOutcome - 1, 3) handles the negative wrap on (Rock, Lose) cleanly and eliminates magic payoff tables.
Reusing MatchupSummary.countOf(opp, derivePlayerShape(opp, outcome)) lets the Part 2 visualizer display the 3x3 target-outcome matrix with zero changes to shared/.

parts.title: Rucksack Reorganization
parts.summary: Split each rucksack string into two equal compartments, find the unique item type present in both halves (a–z = 1–26, A–Z = 27–52), and return the sum of priorities across all rucksacks.
parts.algorithmSummary: 52-bit BigInt bitmask intersection reusing shared/core bigintLog2: immutable Rucksack value objects in 2022/day03/shared/ derive compartment masks dynamically, verify power-of-two uniqueness, and extract 1-based priorities in O(N) time; differentially verified against a Set intersection oracle over 312 rucksacks.
learnings: Using 52-bit BigInt bitmasks with shared/core bigintLog2 avoids JavaScript's 32-bit bitwise truncation on uppercase priorities 32..52 and exposes Rucksack.allMask for Part 2 group intersections.
Keeping Rucksack constructor validation structural (even length and ASCII letters) rather than requiring compartment overlap lets Part 2 reuse Rucksack for arbitrary valid lines.

parts.title: Rucksack Reorganization
parts.summary: Partition the ordered rucksacks into consecutive groups of three Elves, identify the unique item type shared by all three Elves in each group (ignoring compartments), and return the sum of badge priorities.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2022/day03/shared Rucksack.allMask and extractSinglePriority via immutable ElfGroup value objects intersecting a.allMask & b.allMask & c.allMask in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space; differentially verified against a 3-way Set intersection oracle over 156 groups.
learnings: Exposing Rucksack.allMask in 2022/day03/shared let Part 2 compute 3-Elf group badges with a single 3-way BigInt bitwise AND and zero edits to shared/ or part1/.
Passing three explicit Rucksack arguments to ElfGroup's constructor guarantees valid group arity at compile time without dead runtime length branches.

parts.title: Camp Cleanup
parts.summary: Parse pairs of inclusive integer section assignment ranges (a-b,c-d) and count how many pairs have one range completely containing the other.
parts.algorithmSummary: Direct closed-interval endpoint containment scan over immutable AssignmentPair value objects built on shared/core ClosedInterval in 2022/day04/shared/, classifying all 5 PairRelation states dynamically and differentially verified against both sign-product and bitset-subset oracles over 1,000 synthetic pairs.
learnings: Avoid IntervalUnion for pair overlap/containment checks because it coalesces integer-adjacent ranges like [2,3] and [4,5].
Scaling SVG interval bars by totalUnits = bounds.end - bounds.start + 1n in BigInt prevents divide-by-zero on single-point domains and keeps huge ranges exact.

parts.title: Camp Cleanup
parts.summary: Using the same pairs of inclusive integer section assignment ranges (a-b,c-d), count how many pairs overlap at all (sharing at least one section ID).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn closed-interval overlap scan reusing 2022/day04/shared AssignmentPair.overlaps and PairRelation classification in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space; differentially verified against both an endpoint-sweep oracle and a bitset-intersection oracle across 1,000 synthetic pairs.
learnings: Reusing AssignmentPair.overlaps and 5-way PairRelation from 2022/day04/shared delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

Drawing single-point endpoint touches as a distinct diamond marker and only showing a gap bracket when upper.start > lower.end + 1n visually separates overlapping, adjacent-disjoint, and gapped-disjoint ranges.

parts.title: Supply Stacks
parts.summary: Parse an ASCII drawing of numbered crate stacks and a sequence of move commands, simulate CrateMover 9000 lifting crates one at a time (reversing lifted order), and read the top crate label from every stack.
parts.algorithmSummary: Encapsulated in-place stack simulation parameterized by a CraneStrategy interface (CrateMover9000 LIFO reversal) in 2022/day05/shared/ with whitespace-preserving diagram parsing and gravity validation in O(C + K) time; differentially verified against an independent O(S * M) reverse top-crate coordinate tracker across 45 seeded random procedures.
parts.complexity: O(C + K) time, O(S + C) space
learnings: Never .trim() raw input or diagram lines when parsing ASCII crate drawings; leading spaces encode empty left columns while stripped trailing spaces on short lines must still be tolerated.

Parameterizing executeProcedure and traceProcedure by CraneStrategy and placing the pure React Cargo Crane Bay SVG in 2022/day05/shared/viz/ makes Part 2 (CrateMover 9001) zero-churn across both domain and UI.

parts.title: Supply Stacks
parts.summary: Execute the same crate rearrangement procedure with the CrateMover 9001, which lifts count crates as a single contiguous block preserving their vertical order, and read the top crate label from every stack.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn CrateMover9001 CraneStrategy plugging into 2022/day05/shared executeProcedure, traceProcedure, and CraneBayVisualizer: shallow-clones and freezes the lifted bottom-to-top slice intact in O(N + sum(count)) time; differentially verified against an order-preserving O(S * M) backward top-tracker oracle across 50 seeded random procedures.
learnings: Because 2022/day05/shared separated CraneStrategy and placed CraneBayVisualizer in shared/viz/, Part 2 required only 41 lines of domain code and a 15-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to shared/.
Defensive shallow cloning and freezing inside CrateMover9001.arrangeLifted prevents aliasing bugs when direct unit-test callers mutate their source array.

parts.title: Tuning Trouble
parts.summary: Scan a single-line lowercase ASCII datastream buffer to find the 1-based end position of the first contiguous 4-character start-of-packet marker whose characters are all pairwise distinct.
parts.algorithmSummary: Monotonic last-seen jump window parameterized by windowSize in 2022/day06/shared/ using a 26-entry Int32Array (-1 sentinel) in O(N) time and O(1) space independent of window width, paired with a reusable SignalTapeVisualizer in 2022/day06/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against both a Set window oracle and a 26-bit XOR parity oracle (reusing shared/core bitCount) across 60+ PRNG strings.
learnings: Guarding prev >= start in the last-seen jump window prevents stale pre-window duplicates from pulling the left boundary backward while running in O(N) independent of windowSize K.
Parameterizing createMarkerSolver(windowSize) and SignalTapeVisualizer in 2022/day06/shared/ prepares Part 2 (windowSize = 14) with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Tuning Trouble
parts.summary: Scan the same lowercase ASCII datastream buffer to find the 1-based end position of the first contiguous 14-character start-of-message marker whose characters are all pairwise distinct.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2022/day06/shared createMarkerSolver(14) and SignalTapeVisualizer: monotonic last-seen jump window over a 26-entry Int32Array in O(N) time and O(1) space; differentially verified against both a Set window oracle and a BigInt XOR parity oracle (reusing shared/core bitCount) across 40 seeded streams.
learnings: Parameterizing createMarkerSolver(windowSize) and SignalTapeVisualizer in 2022/day06/shared/ reduced Part 2 to 6 lines of domain code and a 14-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to shared/.
Using BigInt masks in the test-only XOR parity oracle (mask ^= 1n << BigInt(code)) plugs directly into shared/core bitCount without 32-bit sign-bit edge cases.

parts.title: No Space Left On Device
parts.summary: Replay a terminal navigation and directory listing transcript to reconstruct the filesystem tree rooted at '/', compute each directory's recursive total size, and sum all directories with total size at most 100,000.
parts.algorithmSummary: Immutable FilesystemTree built from an encapsulated canonical-path builder in 2022/day07/shared/ with single-pass O(D + F) post-order DFS metrics and a reusable log-scaled DirectoryAuditSvg in 2022/day07/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against a path-stack prefix accumulator oracle across 30 seeded random terminal logs up to ~200 directories and depth 9.
learnings: Personal inputs reuse identical directory basenames across unrelated subtrees and even across nested parent/child directories (/a/a), so directories must always be keyed by canonical path or tree-node identity rather than basename.
Log-scaling directory sizes (log10(bytes + 1)) in the shared stacked bar chart keeps 584-byte subdirectories, the 100,000-byte threshold line, and a 48 MB root simultaneously legible.

parts.title: No Space Left On Device
parts.summary: Given a 70,000,000-byte disk requiring at least 30,000,000 bytes of free space, find the smallest single directory whose deletion frees enough space to run the update and return its total size.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn post-order threshold scan reusing 2022/day07/shared FilesystemTree, DirectoryMetrics, and DirectoryAuditSvg: computes minRequiredToDelete = max(0, 30_000_000 - (70_000_000 - rootTotalSize)) and selects the minimum qualifying directory in O(D) time and O(D) space; differentially verified against a path-stack prefix accumulator oracle across seeded random terminal logs.
learnings: Reusing FilesystemTree, DirectoryMetrics, and the log-scaled DirectoryAuditSvg in 2022/day07/shared/ delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.
Handling the already-sufficient-free-space boundary (minRequiredToDelete = 0) and exact-threshold equality (>= rather than >) prevents subtle off-by-one bugs.

parts.title: Treetop Tree House
parts.summary: Given a rectangular 2D grid of single-digit tree heights (0–9), count how many trees are visible from outside the grid along any of the four cardinal lines of sight (all intervening trees strictly shorter).
parts.algorithmSummary: 4-pass strictly-decreasing monotonic stack sightlines engine in 2022/day08/shared/ built on shared/core Grid2D and DIRS_4 with a reusable 10-slot Int32Array stack in O(R * C) time (2.72 ms on 99x99): computes both explicit 4-bit visibilityMask and all 4 Int32Array viewing distances in one pass, paired with a 10-band batched-SVG CanopySightlineSvg visualizer for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified cell-by-cell against a direct DIRS_4 ray-cast oracle across 30 seeded rectangular grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Replacing equal-height entries on the monotonic stack (after recording viewing distance) bounds stack depth to <= 10 across heights 0..9 while tracking visibility explicitly via 4-bit masks to avoid edge-blocker false positives.

Batching 9,801 grid cells into 10 elevation-band SVG <path> elements in 2022/day08/shared/viz/CanopySightlineSvg.tsx keeps 99x99 interactive ray inspection crisp at ~30 SVG DOM nodes and ready for zero-churn Part 2 scenic mode.

parts.title: Treetop Tree House
parts.summary: Compute every tree's scenic score as the product of its four cardinal viewing distances (counting trees up to and including the first tree of equal or greater height, or the grid edge), and return the highest scenic score in the forest.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn monotonic-stack scenic scan reusing 2022/day08/shared ForestGrid, ForestSightlines, and CanopySightlineSvg (mode='scenic'): precomputes all four directional viewing distances in O(R * C) time (3.88 ms on 99x99) and scans interior rows with deterministic row-major tie-breaking via ScenicScanTimeline and ScenicTraceFrame (zero stored derived state); differentially verified against an independent DIRS_4 direct-ray oracle across 60 seeded rectangular grids and 99x99 scale.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Precomputing all four viewing distances inside 2022/day08/shared/ForestSightlines and wiring CanopySightlineSvg mode='scenic' delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.
Evaluating sightlines.scenicScore(row, col) before checking row <= scannedRow inside isInteriorScanned ensures out-of-bounds coordinates always throw RangeError rather than silently returning false.

parts.title: Rope Bridge
parts.summary: Simulate a 2-knot rope (head and tail) starting at (0, 0) under cardinal head motion commands where the tail pulls one orthogonal or diagonal step whenever Chebyshev distance exceeds 1, and count distinct cells visited by the tail.
parts.algorithmSummary: Generalized K-knot Int32Array rope stepper (K = 2) with early-break cascade and polymorphic DenseTailTracker (Uint8Array) / SparseTailTracker (Set<string>) in 2022/day09/shared/ (2.27 ms across ~11,500 head steps), paired with a pure-TS RopeViewport and HiDPI Canvas 2D RopeBridgeVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (K = 10) reuse; differentially verified against an independent point-object + Set<string> oracle across 50 seeded PRNG motion plans and multi-knot diagonal cascades.
parts.complexity: O(M + S * K) time, O(K + min(W * H, V)) space
learnings: Using the unified 16-case Math.sign Chebyshev pull rule and parameterizing knotCount in 2022/day09/shared/ handles both Part 1 (K = 2) and Part 2's (±2, ±2) diagonal cascades (K = 10) with zero shared-module churn.
Keeping knot coordinates in world space and applying (-minX, -minY) shifting solely inside DenseTailTracker avoids shift/unshift boilerplate while bounding dense grid memory to <= 4 MB.

parts.title: Rope Bridge
parts.summary: Extend the rope simulation to 10 knots (head plus 9 trailing knots) starting at (0, 0) under the same cardinal head motions—including (±2, ±2) diagonal cascades—and count distinct cells visited by the 10th knot.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 10-knot specialization (PART2_KNOT_COUNT = 10) reusing 2022/day09/shared Int32Array rope cascade, adaptive DenseTailTracker/SparseTailTracker, and HiDPI Canvas 2D RopeBridgeVisualizer with zero edits to shared/ (2.85 ms across ~11,500 head steps); differentially verified against an independent explicit 4-branch follow oracle covering all 4 (±2, ±2) diagonal quadrants, sparse fallback, and 45 seeded Mulberry32 PRNG plans.
parts.complexity: O(M + S * K) time, O(K + min(W * H, V)) space
learnings: Parameterizing knotCount and implementing the unified Math.sign Chebyshev follow rule in 2022/day09/shared/ reduced Part 2 to 15 lines of production domain code and an 8-line visualizer wrapper with zero shared-module churn.

Asserting that all four (±2, ±2) diagonal cascade quadrants actually fire inside the differential oracle proves Part 2's diagonal pull physics is thoroughly exercised beyond Part 1's orthogonal-head subset.
